name: TSP/HCP Benchmark Set
description: We present a benchmark set for Traveling salesman problem (TSP) with characteristics that are different from the existing benchmark sets. In particular, we focus on small instances which prove to be challenging for one or more state-of-the-art TSP algorithms. These instances are based on difficult instances of Hamiltonian cycle problem (HCP). This includes instances from literature, specially modified randomly generated instances, and instances arising from the conversion of other difficult problems to HCP. We demonstrate that such benchmark instances are helpful in understanding the weaknesses and strengths of algorithms. In particular, we conduct a benchmarking exercise for this new benchmark set totalling over five years of CPU time, comparing the TSP algorithms Concorde, Chained Lin-Kernighan, and LKH. typical_sota_score: 0–5% optimality_gap (many instances solved to optimality; difficult outlier instances can produce small gaps)
reputation: A niche but useful benchmark set in combinatorial optimization for stress-testing TSP/HCP solvers on hard outlier instances.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; focuses on small but unusually hard instances, so results are solver- and instance-dependent and not directly comparable to standard random TSP benchmarks.
